drivingQuestion: Does the mishna already teach the Usha ordinance?
outcomeNote: The suggestion is rejected; the Usha ordinance adds to the mishna.

segments.he: מַתְנִיתִין — בְּחַיֶּיהָ וּלְפֵירוֹת, תַּקָּנַת אוּשָׁא — בְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל קַרְקַע וּלְאַחַר מִיתָה.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: This is not so, as «the mishna» is discussing the husband’s claim «during her lifetime, and» it is referring only «to» the value of «the produce» that the husband collects from the purchasers if she sold the land during their marriage, as the produce of usufruct property belongs to him but the land itself remains fully in the possession of the buyer. «The ordinance of Usha,» in contrast, applies even «to the land itself, and» even «after» the «death» of his wife he may repossess it because he inherits it.

moves.summary: rejects the identification: the two rulings concern different cases
moves.about: the mishna's repossession is during her lifetime and only of the produce

edges.cueHe: מתניתין — בחייה ולפירות, תקנת אושא — בגופה של קרקע
edges.about: rejects the suggestion that the mishna already teaches the Usha ordinance
the mishna's repossession is during her lifetime and only of the produce

positions.claim: the mishna addresses produce during her lifetime; Usha addresses the land after death
